# Current-to-target boundary

## First blocking decision: durable events

Status: resolved for `teacher.decision.recorded`, `learning_action.closed`, `teacher.assistance.observed`, the Student-owned mastery reducer, bounded general/task StudentContext, practice-runtime targets, selected-text lesson verification, the Dialog author/trigger/read/append contract, and durable TeacherOrchestrator runtime. Whole-lesson tutoring without an explicit selection remains out of scope.

See [Student Learning Evidence boundary](current-target-student-evidence-boundary.md) for the implemented reducer, [StudentContext boundary](current-target-student-context-boundary.md) for the mounted task request context, and [TeacherOrchestrator/Dialog boundary](current-target-teacher-dialog-boundary.md) for durable generation/delivery and selected-text lesson policy.

### CURRENT

`ms-go-course` uses optional NATS connectivity and best-effort lifecycle publishing. Some publish failures are ignored and there is no transactional outbox.

### TARGET

Teacher decisions, interventions and learning evidence must be auditable and must not disappear between a committed database change and event publication.

### WHY THIS BLOCKS THE NEXT INCREMENT

Copying the course publisher would violate the product requirement. Introducing an outbox/inbox changes the reliability contract and requires agreement about event ownership, subjects, retry semantics and which service applies mastery evidence.

### ACCEPTED DIRECTION

Keep the `ms-go-course` layer topology, but implement PostgreSQL transactional outbox plus idempotent consumers under `internal/infrastructure/messaging/nats`.

Use a dedicated `TEACHER_EVENTS` JetStream stream and a versioned envelope containing `event_id`, `event_type`, `correlation_id`, `causation_id`, `student_id`, `occurred_at`, `schema_version`, and `data`. Teacher events follow this contract. `ms-go-student` closes actions through its own transactional outbox; teacher-agent consumes the closure durably, finalizes assistance through an inbox/outbox transaction, and Student applies the result asynchronously. Student-facing responses do not wait for evidence or mastery recalculation.

No Knowledge Tree runtime integration is required by these pipelines; target keys remain provider-neutral and owned by their content sources.

## Proactive intervention and analytics

Status: implemented without transferring raw-event or Student-state ownership.

`ms-go-statistic` keeps raw telemetry and emits only bounded interesting
observations. Teacher consumes them durably, resolves a replaceable policy by
`intervention_mode`, records an explainable `intervene` or `stay_silent`
decision, and may append one idempotent consent prompt to the student's general
Dialog per analytics session. Progress stays silent; the default balanced mode
requires three same-error failures over eight active minutes. Student mastery
is not changed by this path.

## Learning-session summaries

Status: implemented as deterministic cross-service orchestration.

Student owns the session lifecycle and its analytics-session link. Statistic
owns active-time and activity aggregation. Teacher reads both exact projections,
formulates a bounded RU/EN summary and pedagogical next step, appends it
idempotently to the same general Dialog, and projects the counters back to the
Student session with optimistic concurrency. No LLM or Knowledge Tree is
required, and the counters do not become mastery evidence.
